subject: recurring-payment
detail: A charges the full slot price once, at booking time, before writing the booking (A-E05). B lets a customer book up to 12 weekly occurrences in one request (B-E02) and says nothing about payment. How a series is paid is undefined.
solutions: Charge every occurrence up front at series creation, one charge per occurrence, all-or-nothing
Save the card and charge each occurrence shortly before it starts
Charge the whole series as one payment
recommended: Charge each occurrence up front at series creation (one Stripe charge per occurrence with its own idempotency key); if any charge fails, refund the ones that succeeded and create nothing. Keeps A's pay-at-booking rule and makes per-occurrence refunds simple. Saved-card charging is deferred (needs stored payment methods and off-session consent).

subject: cancellation-refund
detail: A lets a paid booking be cancelled 24h+ before start but hard-deletes it and issues no refund (A-E03, A-E05); payments.py is missing so a refund elsewhere cannot be ruled out. In the unified app a customer could pay, cancel within the allowed window, and lose the money.
solutions: Full refund on any allowed cancellation (24h+ before start)
recommended: Full refund through Stripe on every allowed cancellation; cancellations under 24h stay refused. Booking becomes status 'cancelled' (not deleted) with the refund id recorded.

subject: waitlist-release
detail: B's waiting list needs to know when a place frees up (B-E05), but A's cancel hard-deletes the booking and emits nothing (A-E03). B does not document whether a freed place is auto-booked (which would charge a card without the customer's consent at that moment) or offered.
solutions: Offer the freed place to the first waiting customer with a time-limited hold; they pay to accept
Auto-book and auto-charge the first waiting customer
Notify everyone on the list; first to pay wins
recommended: Cancellation emits slot-freed; the first waiting customer gets an offer and an exclusive hold (2 hours, ending no later than 24h before start); accepting runs the normal booking and payment flow; expiry passes the offer to the next. No automatic charges.

subject: recurring-cancellation
detail: A's 24h cancellation rule is per booking; B does not say whether a recurring series is cancelled as a whole or per occurrence.
solutions: Each occurrence follows the 24h rule on its own; 'cancel series' cancels every remaining occurrence that is 24h+ away
Series can only be cancelled as a whole before the first occurrence
recommended: Per-occurrence 24h rule; 'cancel series' cancels all remaining occurrences 24h+ away and refunds each.

subject: recurring-partial-availability
detail: B does not say what happens when some weeks of a requested series are already taken.
solutions: All-or-nothing: refuse and list the taken weeks
Book the free weeks and skip the taken ones
recommended: All-or-nothing, listing the taken weeks so the customer can shorten the series or join their waiting lists.

subject: slot-double-booking
detail: A checks slot.taken but never sets it (A-E02), and charges before inserting with no rollback. With recurring bookings and waiting-list offers competing for the same slot, double booking or a charge without a booking is likely.
solutions: Database-enforced single active booking per slot plus hold-then-charge-then-confirm
recommended: A partial unique index on bookings(slot_id) where status in (held, confirmed); create the booking as 'held' inside a transaction, charge, then confirm; on payment failure delete the hold.

subject: accounts-and-roles
detail: Neither source shows authentication: A takes user_id as a parameter (A-E02); B implies two audiences, teams that publish slots and customers that book (B-E01), but documents no auth.
solutions: Email-and-password accounts with roles customer and staff (staff publish slots)
Magic-link sign-in with the same two roles
Delegate to a hosted identity provider
recommended: Email-and-password accounts with server-side sessions in http-only cookies; roles customer and staff; staff manage slots, customers manage only their own bookings and waitlist entries.
